topic: Compile-Time Polymorphism with Template Metaprogramming and its Implementation
explanation: Template metaprogramming allows for compile-time polymorphism, enabling code generation based on template arguments.  This differs drastically from runtime polymorphism (virtual functions) as all computations are performed during compilation.  The compiler uses recursion and template instantiation to generate specialized code for each template argument, essentially eliminating the runtime overhead of virtual function calls. This involves heavy compiler optimization using techniques like constant folding and expression template evaluations, dramatically altering the final assembly.  Memory layout is also affected, as there's no need for virtual function tables (vtables) or dynamic memory allocation for polymorphism. However, excessive template instantiation can lead to code bloat if not managed carefully.  The tradeoff is between compile time and runtime performance.
keywords: Template Metaprogramming, Static Polymorphism, Compile-Time Polymorphism, Static Dispatch
